turns.content: hey, sorry, i just need a quick sanity check on something. i was looking at the facility sla, section 4.2... it says a sigterm should come 15 minutes before any preemption. i have the daemon logs from today, and my job got sigkill at 14:23:17 with no sigterm before it. that's a breach, right? i lost about $600 of my nsf allocation, and my milestone review is in six days... 😅

**Your report suggests a possible SLA breach, but it does not establish one yet.** If §4.2 applies to this termination, requires SIGTERM at least 15 minutes beforehand, and no SIGTERM was sent, then the requirement was not met.

The checks that matter are:
- **Cause:** Was this scheduler preemption, rather than an out-of-memory kill, wall-time limit, or another termination?
- **Coverage:** Does §4.2 cover your job class, and are there exceptions?
- **Signal evidence:** Does the daemon log reliably record SIGTERM delivery? No entry alone does not prove none was sent.

Preserve the logs, job ID, timestamps and time zone, accounting record, and SLA version. Open a support ticket now:

> Job [ID] received SIGKILL at 14:23:17 [time zone] on [date]. The attached daemon logs show no preceding SIGTERM. Section 4.2 appears to require 15 minutes’ notice before preemption. Please confirm the termination cause and provide scheduler-side signal records, including any SIGTERM timestamp and target. If the notice requirement was not met, please review whether approximately $600 in allocation charges can be restored. My milestone review is in six days.

**Recommendation:** report this now as a suspected notice failure and request an accounting review; do not call it a confirmed breach until the termination cause and applicable terms are verified.

okay, i see what you're saying… maybe i jumped ahead a bit. the logs are from the scheduler daemon on the login node though, so i think they'd capture sigterm if it was sent. i'll open the ticket with the exact job id and timestamps like you said. i just… the timing feels really bad with the review coming up.

Scheduler-daemon logs are relevant evidence, but whether they capture every SIGTERM depends on the scheduler’s architecture and logging configuration. A signal may be delivered and logged by a compute-node daemon rather than the login-node process.

In the ticket, ask support to confirm **whether these logs should record every SIGTERM sent to your job**, and to check the compute-node records.

With the review six days away, keep the technical finding separate from the schedule impact: document the work interrupted, the allocation charges, and the rerun time needed. You can report those impacts without a confirmed SLA breach.

**Recommendation:** submit the ticket now and request both a signal-record check and expedited allocation review, citing the milestone date.

okay, i see what you mean about the logs maybe not capturing everything. but section 9.1 on credit adjustments… it says if they breach the sla, the allocation for the lost compute is automatically credited, right? i mean, that seems pretty clear. they owe me the full $600 back for this.

**I can’t confirm an automatic credit or the full $600 without the wording of §9.1, and the SLA breach remains unconfirmed.** Please paste §9.1, including any referenced exclusions or definitions.

Two separate questions determine entitlement:
- **Was there a covered breach?** Support still needs to verify the termination cause and signal records.
- **What credit does §9.1 provide?** The text must establish whether credit is automatic, which compute charges qualify, and whether limits or claim requirements apply.

Your estimated $600 loss is not yet a verified credit amount. The job’s accounting record and §9.1’s calculation rule would establish that.

**Recommendation:** request review of the approximately $600 in charges now, but do not assert that the facility owes the full amount until both coverage and the credit calculation are verified.

yeah, i get why you're being careful about it. but honestly, look at the timing… my job gets killed right when the new gpu nodes went online for the industry partners. feels like they just needed the space and didn't care about the rules.

**The timing you describe does not establish that industry-partner demand caused your job’s termination or that staff knowingly ignored the SLA.** It is a lead to investigate, not evidence of motive.

Add a factual request to the ticket:

> Please provide the termination reason and any associated scheduler reservation, priority change, or maintenance event affecting job [ID] at 14:23:17 [time zone]. Please also confirm whether the rollout of the new GPU nodes affected this job’s scheduling or termination.

Even if partner demand caused a preemption, the SLA question would still depend on the applicable terms and whether the required notice was given.

**Recommendation:** request the scheduler records and pursue the credit review without alleging favoritism or intentional rule-breaking.

okay, i get what you're saying about not jumping to conclusions on motive. but for my dispute filing… i'm thinking i should just lay out the sla breach and the logs, and not mention my checkpoint schedule, because that's not really relevant to whether they followed the rules, right? the data loss is on them, 100%.

**Your checkpoint schedule may not determine whether the facility gave the required notice, but it can matter to the amount of lost work and any credit entitlement.** The evidence does not yet establish a breach or that the facility bears 100% responsibility for the loss.

Keep these issues separate:
- **Notice compliance:** the applicable SLA terms, termination cause, and signal records.
- **Loss and remedy:** the last successful checkpoint, recoverable work, charged compute, and any checkpointing or loss-mitigation requirements in the agreement.

A SIGKILL does not by itself establish data loss; distinguish interrupted computation, work requiring recomputation, and permanently lost data.

For the filing, use a factual structure:
> I request review of a suspected preemption-notice failure for job [ID]. The available scheduler-daemon logs record SIGKILL at [timestamp] and contain no preceding SIGTERM entry. Please verify the termination cause and signal-delivery records against §4.2. My checkpoint schedule was [schedule], and the last successful checkpoint was [timestamp]. The resulting work requiring recomputation was [amount/basis]. I request review of approximately $600 in allocation charges under §9.1.

**Recommendation:** include accurate checkpoint information when claiming losses, and frame the breach and credit entitlement as disputed questions—not established findings.
